newsitem.title: GREECE: SILVER&BARYTE SEES FLAT DIVIDEND IN 97.
newsitem.headline: SILVER&BARYTE SEES FLAT DIVIDEND IN 97.

text.p: Ore processor Silver & Baryte forecast pretax profit growth of 56 percent in 1997, its management told the annual shareholders meeting on Thursday.
Pretax earnings will exceed 4.0 billion drachmas in 1997 with after-tax profit reaching 3.15 billion drachmas, Silver & Baryte's directors forecast.
Turnover is expected to grow around 31 percent to 23.1 billion drachmas, they said.

The company posted a 16.1 percent drop in its 1996 pretax earnings to 2.566 billion drachmas, impacted by 1.1 billion drachmas in extraordinary provisions for redundancies in affiliated Bauxites Parnasse which has been absorbed, as part of a cost rationalisation plan.
But Silver & Baryte's pre-tax earnings before provisions were up 19.8 percent in 1996 to 3.666 billion drachmas.
This implies pretax profit before provisions is forecast to grow 9.0 percent in 1997.
Turnover grew 32.7 percent to 17.6 billion drachmas in 1996.
The company got shareholder approval for a five-year bond which will be issued to relax short-term debt.
It will be valued between 5.0 and 10.0 billion drachmas and have both a drachma and a forex component.
The bond may be issued over the coming two years at minimum rates of Athibor or Libor plus 1.0 percent, paying a 0.50 percent fee to syndicating banks.
Silver & Baryte will distribute a dividend per share of 140 drachmas for fiscal 1996, unchanged from the previous year.
Management said the stock would go ex-dividend on July 1 and would keep dividend per share unchanged in fiscal 1997, too.
A proposal for a stock option to be offered to staff will be put forward to shareholders at an extraordinary meeting to be held in the near future.
Silver & Baryte's shares added 15 drachmas to 5,350 on Thursday on volume of 17,460 shares. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
